# Retained Amalgamation hunt stages

An Amalgamation can choose the same quarry zone in consecutive hunt stages. The confirmed seed 23032 course chose `gen_6` twice: ordinary World completed, while the previous retained runtime refused the second quarry because its materialization marker identified only the event and zone. The original failing course and independent reproduction remain preserved.

`AmalgamationField.minibossIn()` now returns the stage together with the event id and quarry definition from its selected descriptor. `birthPlaceAmalgamMiniboss()` keys the materialization marker as `event:stage@zone`. These are the three bounded runtime edits in two files; quarry death handling, rewards, choices, timing, random draws and save format remain unchanged.

A new stage may furnish its own quarry even when it selects visited ground. Re-entering the same stage retains the actual wounded quarry without duplication. No area, peer, unrelated body or wound census is reset. The actual peer course covers idle, downed and dead party occupants and hosted road transfers through the repeated target. A held dead quarry reference cannot advance the replacement hunt or pay again; the existing combat guards supply that behavior.

Cold Continue follows the existing original policy: restore the active event, stage, chosen parts, character identity and reward ledger, then reconstruct one fresh current quarry. Local event-body wounds are not serialized by this change. The independent launcher/save course compares empty original and retained child processes from the same real stage-1 save, verifies one fresh quarry without duplicates, and advances both through the actual kill and graft to stage 2. Warm wound preservation and cold reconstruction are deliberately distinct observations.

Acceptance uses the original paired negative (230), bounded runtime candidate (233), independent peer/cold review (232), and composition over accepted Fracture (227/231). Paired seed 23032 repeated-target and seed 23031 distinct-target journeys complete through three parts and the boss; retained return checks preserve quarry wounds. Run `nativeamalgamationstages` with `--wounds`, its `--world` controls, `nativeamalgamationpeers`, `nativeamalgamationcold`, and `nativeamalgamationstagesource`, plus the existing Fracture/Vendetta source and overlap checks and all four type checks.

The tests use the actual Bonewright opening, dwell, native combat deaths and part choices; fixture-controlled travel, clock advancement and player invulnerability make them bounded headless courses. They are not browser, TCP reconnect, deployment-capacity or complete-content-parity acceptance. The inherited standalone installed-source graph assertion remains red and unchanged. Private quest areas, generated entrances, terrain layouts and Shards capacity remain separate work.
